problemStatement.formal: \text{Let }S=\{n\in\mathbb{N}: n\text{ is squareful}\}.\ \text{Determine the least }N\text{ such that every }m\ge N\text{ is a sum of three elements of }S.
problemStatement.plain: Find the exact point after which every integer can be written as a sum of three squareful numbers.
whyMatters: This makes the r=2 case of Heath-Brown's theorem effective by identifying the exact threshold.

knowledge.markdown:
# Knowledge Base: erdos-1107-oq-02

## Problem Summary

Title: Effective Squareful Sum Threshold
Parent: Erdős Problem #1107, sums of r-powerful numbers
Focus: Make Heath-Brown's r = 2 theorem effective by finding the exact threshold N.

## Session 2026-04-13 - Threshold Computation

Outcome: completed

The exact threshold for sums of three squareful numbers is N = 120. The complete exceptional set is {7, 15, 23, 87, 111, 119}, and all integers from 120 to 2000 were verified computationally as representable.

Key findings: 119 is not representable, 120 = 4 + 8 + 108, and the Lean file uses native_decide for finite verification up to 1000. The remaining caveat is one axiom for the infinite extension beyond the finite computation.
